subtopics.title: The Spaza Shop Cash Box (Intro to VAT)

questions.question: What does a VAT inclusive amount represent?
options: The original price of the item plus the 15% VAT added to it (115%).
The amount of tax the business gets to keep as profit (15%).
Only the original price of the item before tax was added (100%).
The amount of tax paid directly to SARS by the customer (15%).

questions.question: If an item is marked 'R115 including VAT', what is the VAT exclusive amount?
Who does the VAT collected by a business belong to?
options: The customer who bought the item.

questions.question: An item is marked R4 600 including VAT at 15%. What is the correct calculation to find the VAT amount?
A customer pays R1 380 for goods, including VAT. What is the VAT amount?
Using the same amount (R1 380 including VAT), what is the VAT exclusive price of the goods?
When goods are sold for cash, which account is debited with the VAT inclusive amount?
In a cash sale transaction of R2 875 (inclusive of R375 VAT), what is the correct credit entry for Sales?
Why is VAT Control credited when goods are sold?
options: Because the business owes that VAT amount to SARS, creating a liability.
Because VAT collected is an extra income for the business.
Because VAT decreases the owner's equity.
Because VAT Control is an asset account increasing.
